To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the momentum diffusion coefficient of a heavy quarked in a quark-gluon plasma can be defined in terms of a certain Euclidean correlator, and that in perturbation theory, the spectral function corresponding this correlator is rather broad, which makes the determination of this coefficient on the lattice a promising possibility.

the heavy quark momentum diffusion coefficient in the large quark mass limit can be defined through the correlator of the electric field and the Polyakov loop, and that this correlator can be computed on a lattice with relatively little systematic uncertainty, and that the thermalization time is inversely proportional to this coefficient.

the heavy quark momentum diffusion coefficient can, in the large-momentum limit, be defined through a correlation function involving color-electric field along a Polyakov line, that this correlation function is relatively insensitive to analytic continuation, and that this correlation function can be computed on the lattice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the heavy quarks in a thermal bath.
the determination of the quark-thermalization rate from the heavy quark momentum diffusion coefficient, which is related to the correlator of the Polyakov loop and the chromoelectric field.
the thermalization of heavy quarks in the quark-gluon plasma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thermalization rate of heavy quarks can be determined with a relatively small systematic error from lattice data.
the heavy quark diffusion coefficient is not well determined, but the heavy quark momentum diffusion coefficient can, in principle, be determined with relatively good accuracy.
the heavy quark diffusion coefficient can be estimated from the lattice, at least to a good approximation, by using the Euclidean correlator of Polyakov loop and color-electric field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the heavy quark limit, the thermalization rate can be extracted from the lattice with relatively small errors, and the results would be in agreement with the weak coupling perturbative prediction, if the lattice is fine enough to resolve the small frequency behavior of the correlation function.
the thermalization of the heavy quarks in the quark-gluon plasma can be studied with lattice QCD, and the result is expected to be reliable.
the momentum diffusion coefficient of a heavy quarks in the quark-gluon plasma can be determined from a lattice calculation of the correlator of a Polyakov loop with a color-electric field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a precise lattice computation of the momentum diffusion coefficient of a heavy quarks would allow one to determine the thermalization rate of the plasma.
the momentum diffusion coefficient of a heavy quarks is related to the correlator involving the color-electric field and Polyakov loop in the static limit.
the thermalization rate can be estimated with reasonable accuracy from the Euclidean lattice data, without the need to resort to analytic continuation.
